name: Banking system stress
summary: Stress gauges below Watch lines: St Louis Fed index -0.07, up from -0.87, and ECB indicator 0.029; no bank failure found
state: The St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index rose to -0.07 in the week to 20 Nov from -0.87 a week earlier, still below the 0 Watch line (FRED). The ECB's systemic stress indicator was 0.029 on 24 Nov, far below 0.25 (ECB). This run's searches to 26 Nov found no mid-sized or larger bank failure, rescue or emergency facility. The US index is near its Watch line after the November equity sell-off.
for_you: Bank deposits and payments are working normally. UK deposits are protected up to the FSCS limit.
rubric_hit: STLFSI -0.07 below the 0 Watch line; ECB CISS 0.04 below the 0.25 Watch line

sources.title: FRED — St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index
ECB Data Portal — Composite Indicator of Systemic Stress

why: Bank failures turn market losses into credit crunches; 2008 and 2023 both began as 'contained' bank problems.
drivers: Rate shocks to bond portfolios, commercial property losses, deposit flight, private-credit links.

rubric.alert: STLFSI > 1.5, or ECB CISS > 0.45, or a systemically important bank fails or needs rescue, or emergency central-bank facilities launched.
rubric.watch: STLFSI 0–1.5, or ECB CISS 0.25–0.45, or a mid-sized bank failure/rescue, or a large bank under visible funding pressure.
rubric.normal: St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index < 0, ECB CISS < 0.25, and no notable bank failures or rescues.
